items.title: Trump 'completely wrong' to restrict support for Ukraine, Italian minister tells BBC
items.summary: Defence Minister Guido Crosetto tells the BBC the US risks prolonging Russia's full-scale invasion rather than helping to end it.
items.content:
Italy's defence minister has said it is a "complete mistake, a major mistake" for the US to limit access to satellite systems and intelligence used by Ukraine to defend itself against Russian attacks.

In a BBC interview, Guido Crosetto warned that any such move by US President Donald Trump's administration "makes absolutely no sense" and risked prolonging Russia's full-scale invasion rather than helping to bring peace.

US officials have said Trump has not asked for the slowdown of internet speeds the US provides to Ukraine and which are vital for its war effort. Trump has also denied that the US has stopped sharing early-warning alerts of incoming Russian aerial attacks with Ukraine.

Crosetto's comments continue Italy's sharpening criticism of the US.

Earlier this week, Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni called Trump's deal to buy diesel from Russia a "very risky choice", and said it would "grant Russia legitimacy" as it bombed cities in Ukraine.

Trump agreed the deal with Vladimir Putin, blaming Kyiv's own attacks on Russian refineries for rising fuel prices.

Meloni, once considered so close to the US president she was dubbed a "Trump whisperer", said the move ran counter to efforts to bring Putin to the negotiating table.

"Peace will come when Putin is convinced there is a stalemate, that he cannot advance any further," her defence minister told the BBC at his ministry building in Rome.

Crosetto was a co-founder of Meloni's hard-right Fratelli d'Italia party, which has led a right-wing government coalition since 2022, shortly after the start of Russia's full-scale war.

"If [Putin] sees weakness on the Ukrainian side – and if the US deprives Ukraine of resources, that creates weakness – then he will believe he can win. So he will continue the war," Crosetto warned.

Despite widespread public scepticism, Meloni's Italian government has been a strong ally of Ukraine from the start, sending both military and humanitarian aid.

The specifics of those deliveries have always been classified.

In our interview, the defence minister vowed that Italian military support would continue "for as long as this government is in place", though he warned that getting parliament to approve further deliveries would be "more difficult" as elections approached.

The vote has to take place by the end of 2027 and opinion polls currently put a new far-right party, Futuro Nazionale, ahead of all Meloni's coalition partners.

Zelensky says Ukraine has right to defend itself after Trump calls latest strikes a 'disgrace'

Inside Ukrainian offensive pushing Russia back - with Starlink playing a key role

That party's leader, former general Roberto Vannacci, is openly sympathetic to Russia and opposes aiding Ukraine, arguing that Europe is wasting its money as Russia's military "continues to advance" on the ground.

At a recent event in Tuscany, he described himself as "neither pro-Putin nor pro-Russian" but "pro-Italian".

Crosetto brushed off questions about Vannacci, including on whether his views reflected those of many Italians, saying he had more "serious matters to deal with".

But, perhaps to underline the difference, he was unequivocal on Russia.

"When one state crosses another state's border with tanks, when it bombs hospitals and schools, kills civilians and bombs power plants, and has been doing so for four years, I can only describe that as evil," he said.

But Italians, like many Europeans, are seeing prices go up, driven by the high cost of energy.

During street protests in Rome on Friday, where firecrackers were thrown, secondary school students complained that resources were being diverted to arms, instead of education.

In southern Italy, truckers have begun blocking roads complaining at the hike in fuel prices.

Polls here regularly show that a majority of Italians want an end to military aid for Ukraine. One, conducted for the Ixè institute in September, put support for continuing to supply arms at just 18%.

There are many factors behind that, from a long-standing pacifist tradition to a history of strong business ties to Moscow. Unlike Poland or the Baltic states, Italy feels physically distant from the danger, too.

But the defence minister also blamed an active campaign of disinformation by Moscow – targeting, he said, "certain political figures... and narratives to weaken the political climate against Russia".

"In some way they shift public opinion," the minister argued.

"It's very hard to explain to a citizen who's having trouble at the petrol pump that we can't give any concessions to Russia right now. But that's the only way to defend the future of that very citizen who's complaining."

Italy has not been targeted for major acts of sabotage, unlike other allies of Ukraine in Europe.

The minister said a fire at an arms depot outside Rome in August was not arson, but "human stupidity".

A report last month that Russia was planning to launch drone attacks at Italy, France and Spain from the container ships in the Mediterranean was not proven, Crosetto also told us.

But cyber-attacks, which he linked to Russia, were now routine - "there are hundreds every day" - and he believed Europe had been too weak in its response.

"You can't win a war... if you don't fight back," the minister said.

items.title: Pope pictured for first time since surgery and cancer diagnosis
items.summary: The pontiff was diagnosed with lung cancer after having surgery at Rome's Gemelli Hospital on Tuesday.
items.content:
Pope Leo XIV has been pictured celebrating Mass from hospital, in the first images of him released by the Vatican since he underwent lung surgery.

The 71-year-old pontiff was diagnosed with lung cancer after the surgery at Rome's Gemelli Hospital on Tuesday afternoon, which the Vatican said had been "successful" and proceeded without complications.

The images shared on Friday showed the Chicago-born Pope wearing a green robe while standing behind a makeshift altar on the tenth floor of the hospital.

Pope Leo "celebrated with the medical and nursing staff" and thanked workers for their service, the Vatican press office said.

Pope's cancer diagnosis leaves Catholics questioning what comes next

Also on Friday, the Pope phoned Russian President Vladimir Putin from hospital to urge a ceasefire in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky, where access to food and water has been cut off for thousands .

"The fact that he accepted the call and spoke with the Pope may, I hope, be a sign that the Pope's request will indeed be carried out," said Cardinal Pietro Parolin, the Vatican's secretary of state.

Without mentioning a ceasefire, the Kremlin said: "The Vatican's intention to help create the conditions necessary to ensure the safety of the town's population and to organise vital supplies has been supported".

The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, Volker Turk, made a similar plea to address what he described as a "desperate" situation in Oleshky.

The Pope's doctors said on Friday tests had shown "a steady improvement in his general condition" since his surgery.

His doctors said that a chest X-ray indicated "good recovery of the operated lung".

The whole lower lobe of the Pope's right lung was removed "to ensure the procedure was radical", the Vatican said following the surgery.

"After the operation, the Pope awoke normally and returned after a brief period of observation to his room," it said earlier, before he spent a "peaceful night" at the hospital.

Pope Leo first announced that he would be having the operation during his weekly Sunday prayers, telling the crowd in St Peter's Square that doctors had found a "well-contained" nodule on his lung "at an early stage" and advised him to have it removed.

Nodules are quite common and not necessarily cancerous, but after it was examined the medical team confirmed it was, "as suspected by pre-operative tests", the Vatican said. He was diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma.

The Vatican has stressed that the Pope had shown no symptoms of infection or illness prior to the procedure.

Pope diagnosed with lung cancer but had successful surgery, Vatican says

items.title: Oregon teacher fought school attacker before armed dad shot suspect 'multiple times'
items.summary: The 16-year-old suspect previously attended the primary school and had targeted a special educational needs classroom, police say.
items.content:
An Oregon teacher threw her mobile phone before she tackled and tried to wrestle away a shotgun from the arms of a teen suspect who opened fire on a special educational needs class.

As she tussled with him on the floor of the class - where three children and a teacher were killed - a bystander ran inside. Armed with a .40-caliber pistol, he opened fire and killed the teen.

The bystander, a dad of two girls at the school, had been driving past Silver Rail Elementary in Bend when he saw the suspect firing in the car park then shooting through a window to enter.

The details of the Thursday attack were confirmed by police, who said the 16-year-old suspect was a prior student at the school.

Police say the suspect was armed with about 44 more rounds of shotgun ammunition when he was stopped. He fired as many as 15 rounds in the class.

"To the people who showed courage in the face of such violence, and intervened to prevent this tragedy from being any worse, we owe you a debt of gratitude," Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz said on Friday.

Police offered more information on the attack at at a news conference on Friday, where they identified two of the four victims. They include five-year-old Rhoam Summer and 25-year-old teacher Meghan Lambert.

The families of the two other students who were killed, an eight-year-old and 11-year-old, did not wish to have them publicly identified yet, police said.

Two others were injured in the attack. Another teacher, a 54-year-old, was still being treated at hospital, and a seven-year-old student, who was in serious but stable condition.

Krantz said the heroic actions of both the teacher and the father who ran inside the school saved lives.

He said the teacher who wrestled with the gunman was not hurt but "almost certainly helped prevent more bloodshed".

He identified the suspect as 16-year-old Griffin J. John II, who previously attended the school and was a special educational needs student there.

A search warrant has been executed at the suspect's home and a search is ongoing, the police chief said.

Police believe the suspect travelled to the elementary school on foot, but police are still investigating his exact movements and how he acquired the gun. A motive is also not clear.

Officials did not confirm the name of the father who intervened and fatally shot the suspect.

But Kaylub Giamanco's family has identified him to US media as the person who sprang into action.

The 36-year-old carpenter had just finished lunch and was on his way home when he passed the school, his brother told NBC News. He saw the suspect open fire on a vehicle outside the school then shoot through a window and go inside.

Police said he had a legally concealed .40 caliber in his vehicle and his brother said he grabbed the pistol "and decided to go in after" the suspect. Police say he fired at the suspect "multiple times", killing him.

In a statement to the BBC's partner CBS News, Giamanco's family said he is a "lifelong resident of Bend" and that he "is not seeking recognition".

The family said Giamanco wants to express his "gratitude to the first responders, school personnel, and community for the outpouring of love and support". He and his family "respectfully ask for privacy".

US President Donald Trump praised the bystander's actions on Friday, calling him a "great hero".

Addressing reporters at the White House before departing for Georgia, Trump said the situation could have been "much worse" with no intervention.

"It's a terrible thing, but thank goodness for a man that had a gun and knew how to use it," he said.

Without naming the bystander, Governor Kotek acknowledged the man's heroic actions stopping further loss of life, but noted they "carry a heavy emotional burden, and I just want you to know that my thoughts are with you as well".

items.title: Trial of German steakhouse heiress that sparked a huge spy scandal
items.summary: For 15 months, a high-security courtroom in Hamburg has been hearing the case of Christina Block, accused of ordering the abduction of her children.
items.content:
It is a trial that has gripped Germany, with a wealthy heiress in the dock for months and a case that triggered the country's biggest espionage scandal in recent history.

Christina Block, heir to a popular chain of steakhouses, is accused of ordering an Israeli security firm to carry out the violent abduction of her children from Denmark, following a bitter custody battle with her former husband.

There are allegedly connections with at least two former secret agents, from Germany and Israel.

In the latest twist, investigators in the case stumbled across evidence that has led to Germany's former intelligence chief, August Hanning, being arrested this month for treason and espionage.

Hanning's arrest stunned the intelligence community. Although his case has nothing to do with the Hamburg trial, he has denied allegations of involvement in an earlier attempted abduction of the children.

There was enormous media interest in Germany when Christina Block and six others went on trial in a high-security courtroom in Hamburg in July last year.

Block House restaurants, specialising in steak and baked potatoes, are a feature of many German towns. Their success over the past half century has helped make Christina Block's father Eugen a multimillionaire.

Prosecutors allege that she and a family lawyer, Andreas Costard, organised the forcible abduction of two of her children, who were staying with her former husband, Stephan Hensel, at his home in Denmark.

They say the operation was carried out by a 36-year-old Israeli citizen named only as Jonathan G and five others.

The abduction took place during the New Year celebrations of 2023-24, as the two children and their father were watching a firework display, according to the indictment.

Prosecutors say several men ambushed and beat up Stephan Hensel, and dragged the boy and the girl, then 10 and 13 years old, into a car.

On the approach to the border with Germany, they are alleged to have changed vehicles, taped up the children's mouths and tied the girl's hands.

The group are then said to have travelled on to Baden-Württemberg in a campervan. Prosecutors say the children were held there against their will until their mother arrived to pick them up on 2 January 2024 and took them to her home in Hamburg.

Christina Block, Andreas Costard and Jonathan G are charged with the abduction of minors, grievous bodily harm and unlawful detention.

Block's partner, a former TV sports presenter called Gerhard Delling, and three others are charged with aiding and abetting.

All of them deny wrongdoing, except for Jonathan G, who has admitted his involvement. However, he told the court he thought he was taking part in a rescue operation.

The trial comes after years of legal battles between Christina Block and her former husband, Stephan Hensel, over who had the right to look after the children.

Immediately after their separation, all four children lived with their mother in Hamburg. Hensel, who remarried, later moved to Denmark, where they regularly visited him.

In 2021, the two youngest children went to visit their father in Denmark, but then were not brought back to Hamburg as agreed.

A court in Hamburg ruled that Christina had custody and that the children should be returned. However, in February 2023, a Danish court ruled that, although the boy and the girl had been brought to Denmark unlawfully, they could not be taken back.

In May 2023, Hensel was charged with the abduction of minors, in a case which is still pending.

He has accused Christina of being violent with the children, charges she denies. She told the court Hensel wanted to take revenge on her.

She also denied knowing anything about plans for the abduction of the children from Denmark. Her defence argues that the Israeli security team had acted on its own initiative.

She told the court it was "a catastrophe" and that she had never wanted anything like that.

The head of the Israeli security team, David Barkay, who is not on trial but faces future legal proceedings, told the court that Christina Block and Costard had known about the planned repatriation operation.

Barkay, who was described by another witness as a former agent with Mossad, the Israeli secret service, said he had not shared all the details because he "didn't trust them."

The alleged connection with Germany's former spy chief, August Hanning, relates to accusations of an earlier attempt to abduct the children and bring them back from Denmark in 2022.

Prosecutors have said Hanning was responsible for arranging security staff sent to Denmark with Christina Block. His lawyer denies the accusations. Hanning has not been charged over the current Block court case.

However, while investigators were searching his home, they came across evidence to suggest Hanning was involved in buying some 2,000 documents from his former chief of staff and then passing on state secrets to foreign powers.

Which foreign power and who he is alleged to have given the secrets to is unspecified, but it has prompted widespread speculation.

Now 80, Hanning is in custody charged with treasonous espionage. His lawyer says he is being "unjustly persecuted" and that the charges are "unfounded".

Meanwhile the trial against Christina Block is currently on hold for two weeks - one of numerous delays and extensions over the course of the past 15 months.

The latest delay is because a witness, Stephan Hensel's new wife, failed to appear in court.

items.title: Il Papa sente Putin e chiede tregua per Oleshky, lo zar apre
items.summary: Trump, 'Putin ascolterà il Papa per far finire la guerra? Credo anche lui lo voglia'
items.content:
Il Papa è tornato nel pieno del lavoro. Le sue condizioni migliorano, anche se è ancora un paziente in fase post-operatoria. Ma ha ripreso in mano completamente tutti i dossier politici. A partire dal conflitto tra Russia e Ucraina. E dal Gemelli, dove è ricoverato, ha telefonato al presidente russo Vladimir Putin al quale ha chiesto una tregua per la cittadina di Oleshky sotto assedio, incassando l'apertura del presidente russo. I due si erano già sentiti a giugno dello scorso anno, il Papa ha più volte offerto la Santa Sede per eventuali negoziati e recentemente ha inviato a Mosca due suoi alti collaboratori.

"Credo che anche lui voglia finire la guerra". Così Donald Trump ha replicato alla domanda se, dopo che Papa Leone ha parlato in una telefonata con Vladimir Putin per far finire la guerra in Ucraina, il presidente russo ascolterà le parole del pontefice. "Gli auguriamo ogni bene. Ho parlato con suo fratello. Suo fratello è una gran brava persona, è un mio amico, e gli ho detto: 'Per favore, porga i miei migliori auguri'". ha poi detto Trump rispondendo a una domanda se parlerà con papa Leone, poco prima di lasciare la Casa Bianca.

Nel frattempo il Vaticano ha diffuso le prime sue foto dopo l'intervento, dove appare in forma , ha confermato che il decorso post-operatorio procede bene e che il Papa, tra una fisioterapia e l'altra, lavora. Confermato anche l'Angelus di domenica , verosimilmente dal policlinico Gemelli. Ma resta anche aperta l'ipotesi di una dimissione dall'ospedale anticipata a domani e in quel caso Leone parlerà a Piazza San Pietro, come la scorsa domenica quando ha annunciato al mondo il suo problema di salute.

Papa Leone XIV ha avuto dunque un colloquio telefonico con il presidente della Federazione Russa e ha espresso tutta la sua "viva preoccupazione per la grave situazione umanitaria nella città di Oleshky, nella regione di Kherson, chiedendo una tregua per consentire l'arrivo di aiuti alimentari e sanitari e l'evacuazione volontaria e sicura della popolazione civile". Il Santo Padre, fa sapere la sala stampa vaticana, "ha infine ribadito l'impegno della Santa Sede a favore del dialogo e della pace". Dal Cremlino arriva una mano tesa: Putin ha fornito a Papa Leone "spiegazioni complete circa la responsabilità del regime di Kiev per la difficile situazione umanitaria" creatasi nella città di Oleshky evocata dal pontefice. Ma ha comunque assicurato sostegno per "l'intenzione del Vaticano di aiutare a creare condizioni per assicurare la sicurezza della popolazione della città e organizzare le forniture vitali". Parole dove in controluce, secondo chi da tempo segue il dossier, si può leggere che potrebbe essere lo stesso Vaticano a mettere in campo, o comunque a sostenere, il ponte umanitario. A spiegare la dinamica della telefonata di oggi è stato il cardinale Segretario di Stato Pietro Parolin: "E' stato il Santo Padre che ha preso l'iniziativa per perorare la causa di questa città assediata nella quale si trovano circa duemila civili che hanno bisogno di canali per l'uscita, di canali umanitari. Il Papa credo abbia chiesto che ci sia una tregua per permettere sia l'arrivo di aiuti umanitari, soprattutto cibo, sia anche l'evacuazione di coloro che devono uscire dalla città". Si è aperta dunque una finestra di dialogo, se pur su un punto specifico, che potrebbe portare a dei passi in avanti. Questo era d'altronde trapelato dopo le recenti missioni a Mosca di monsignor Paul Richard Gallagher, il 'ministro degli esteri' vaticano, e il cardinale Matteo Zuppi, che tanto si è impegnato sulle questioni umanitarie, dallo scambio di prigionieri al ritorno a casa dei bambini ucraini che erano stati portati in territorio russo. Un 'pressing', quello della diplomazia vaticana, che vuole arrivare a tutti i costi ad un risultato. Se la pace è comunque l'obiettivo finale, ci sono le tante questioni umanitarie da risolvere subito. E sempre nello storico Angelus di domenica scorsa, l'11, quello dell'annuncio del nodulo, Leone aveva espresso tutta la sua preoccupazione, per esempio, per il blocco del transito dei cereali nel Mar Nero. Il Papa c'è. E' ligio alle indicazioni mediche, seguirà i consigli di chi lo ha preso in cura. Ma resta il Papa che governa, che sta mettendo mano alle nomine di peso, che è sul ponte di comando anche sullo scacchiere geopolitico. Proseguono anche i preparativi per il viaggio in Sudamerica: è uscita la lista dei giornalisti ammessi al volo. Non è una conferma ufficiale ma comunque indirettamente si ribadisce che il Papa vuole andare. Ora tutto dipenderà solo dalle indicazioni dei medici.

items.title: La tripletta di Raimondo fa volare il Frosinone, 4-2 al Sassuolo CRONACA E FOTO
items.summary: Il bomber è il nuovo capocannoniere della Serie A. Tra i neroverdi male Muric
items.content:
Frosinone batte Sassuolo 4-2 nell'anticipo della settima giornata di Serie A

Frosinone-Sassuolo 4-2 al 57' rete di Antonio Raimondo! Cala il tris personale l'attaccante della squadra di Alvini, abile ad avventarsi sul pallone dopo un colpo di testa di Ghedjemis ispirato dal cross di Kvernadze. Parata iniziale di Muric, con nessuno dei neroverdi che protegge la zona vicina alla porta: il centravanti dei ciociari è al posto giusto nel momento giusto. Sale a 7 gol, ora è virtualmente capocannoniere, nella Serie A

Frosinone-Sassuolo 3-2 al 37'! Rete di Kristian Thorstvedt ! Accorciano le distanze i neroverdi: Esposito viene incontro a prendere la palla, si gira imbucando per il suo compagno che a tu per tu con Palmisani lo infila con un diagonale preciso.

Frosinone-Sassuolo 3-1 al 30'! Altro errore di Muric che non legge bene un campanile creato da Caleta-Car lasciando a disposizione il pallone: Raimondo fiuta la chance ruba il pallone e deposita nella porta vuota. Ora la squadra di Alvini può gestire un doppio vantaggio.

Frosinone-Sassuolo 2-1 al 26'! Rete di Antonio Raimondo! Pasticcio di Muric che in uscita, su un cross proveniente da destra, si perde il pallone nel cuore dell'area di rigore: Raimondo è il più lesto di tutti a capire la situazione a timbrare il gol del nuovo vantaggio dei ciociari. Il suo quinto gol nella Serie A

Frosinone-Sassuolo 1-1 al 15'! Rete di Domenico Berardi! Sbilanciato in avanti il Frosinone si fa trovare scoperto sulla fascia destra: verticalizzazione immediata di Bakola che trova il capitano dei neroverdi: a tu per tu con Palmisani, qualche finta e un rimpallo per saltarlo e poi il tocco finale a porta vuota vale il punto del pareggio.

Frosinone-Sassuolo1-0 al 9'! Rete di Giacomo Calò! Bakola cerca la costruzione dal basso gestendo in maniera prolungata il pallone all'interno della propria area di rigore: il giocatore dei neroverdi sulla pressione del Frosinone perde palla in un contatto lasciandola a disposizione del centrocampista del Frosinone che a pochi metri dalla porta non sbaglia siglando il vantaggio dei padroni di casa.

La sconfitta di Napoli può essere derubricata a incidente di percorso . Il Frosinone si riscatta subito, batte il Sassuolo e riprende l'ottimo cammino interrotto al Maradona sabato scorso. Alvini e soci salgono a quota 13 raggiungendo il Cagliari al quarto posto addirittura in zona Champions, trascinati dal giovane centravanti Raimondo, autore di una tripletta (la prima in Serie A) e nuovo capocannoniere del campionato a quota 7.

Per i ciociari è la terza vittoria di fila in casa e guardano con grande fiducia al proseguo della stagione. Il Sassuolo è invece alla terza sconfitta in campionato, che conferma le difficoltà degli emiliani in trasferta dove hanno racimolato appena 1 punto in 4 partite: la vittoria manca dal torneo passato, 15 febbraio, 1-2 a Udine. Aquilani resta fermo a 8 con più di qualche punto interrogativo a partire dal portiere Muric protagonista in negativo della partita con errori decisivi sui gol del Frosinone. Alvini conferma per 10/11 la formazione battuta a Napoli: al centro della difesa rientra Monterisi dopo la panchina a Napoli, fuori Calvani. Due novità nel Sassuolo rispetto al match pareggiato col Milan: tra i centrali Odenthal sostituisce l'infortunato Leysen; in mezzo al campo dentro Thorsvedt, fuori Adzic. Prima del fischio d'inizio premiati Alvini e Raimondo (segno del destino) rispettivamente come miglior allenatore e miglior under 23 dei mesi di agosto e settembre . La curva dei tifosi ciociari vuota per i primi 15': i sostenitori protestano per la gestione dell'ordine pubblico durante la trasferta di Napoli che avrebbe "calpestato la dignità delle persone".

Subito ritmi alti e partenza forte di entrambe le squadre. Pochi tatticismi e tanti errori, grandi spazi e ribaltamenti di fronte. Il Sassuolo s'affida al palleggio e al gioco corto, il Frosinone al pressing martellante e agli strappi dei suoi attaccanti. Già al 5' chance per Thorstvedt che non trova il tempo di calciare dopo l'azione di Bakola. Il Frosinone risponde con lo spunto di Ghedjemis al 7': tiro di poco alto. Preludio al vantaggio: al 9' errore di Bakola che al limite dell'area si fa soffiare il pallone da Masini con Calò bravo a siglare il suo secondo gol stagionale. Il Sassuolo risponde dopo soli 6 minuti: Bakola si fa perdonare e con un lancio lungo trova Berardi smarcato. L'attaccante s'invola e batte Palmisani indeciso nell'uscita. La sarabanda continua al 17': Kvernadze firma il sorpasso ma è in fuorigioco. La partita è sempre più pazza con due difese troppo allegre.

E così al 27' Muric fa la frittata: non trattiene il lancio di Calò e Raimondo ne approfitta per siglare il 2-1. Passano 3' e il film si ripete: altra topica di Muric che sbaglia l'uscita di testa e Raimondo cala il tris. Il doppio vantaggio non demoralizza il Sassuolo che al 37' accorcia: filtrante di Esposito , Oyono è troppo morbido e rete di Thorstvedt. Primo tempo in archivio con 5 reti, tante azioni e poco equilibrio. Nella ripresa ci si aspetta un Sassuolo arrembante per cercare il pari, invece è il Frosinone ad avere qualcosa in più. I ciociari sono pericolosi al 6' con Schmid (parata di Muric) e all'11' con Kvernadze (conclusione ribattuta). Il poker è nell'aria e lo centra al 12' il solito Raimondo bravo a ribadire in rete la respinta corta di Muric sul colpo di testa di Ghedjemis: tripletta e pallone nella vetrinetta di casa

Il Frosinone non è sazio e al 20' Calò chiama all'intervento Muric. Girandola di cambi da una parte e dall'altra, il Sassuolo prova a rientrare in partita ma il Frosinone è più compatto e non si sorprendere. Ci provano comunque Lipani al 31' (esterno rete) e Laurientè al 34' (parata di Palmisani). Sono gli ultimi veri sussulti della partita che regala 3 punti pesanti al Frosinone e consegna al campionato il nuovo capocannoniere: Antonio Raimondo.

items.title: Katie Zacharia leaving her White House role less than five days on the job
items.summary: Her public debut as White House press secretary on Tuesday ended with a flurry of media criticism about her credentials and preparedness.
items.content:
Katie Zacharia will be leaving her post as White House press secretary, the BBC has confirmed, as the fallout from her shaky public debut appears to have reached its climax.

Speaking to reporters moments before news of her exit dropped on Friday, President Donald Trump said he had told her "you don't have to do this if you don't want to" and "honestly, if I were you, I'd reconsider".

Zacharia faced heavy criticism for her first press briefing in the role on Tuesday, which lasted less than 15 minutes and included only three questions from reporters.

She spent the days after playing defence, answering tough questions from news outlets about her credentials and preparedness for the job.

Trump hinted at her impending exit early on Friday afternoon, during a press gaggle outside Marine One.

"I said, 'Is this for you, Katie? Because honestly, you don't need this," Trump said.

"You don't have to be treated this badly," he continued, adding that he believed she had been treated "pretty nastily" by the media.

The BBC confirmed she was leaving the job a few hours later.

As the country draws closer to the November midterm elections, which will decide who controls the US Congress, Democrats are seizing on Zacharia's abrupt departure as a sign of failure in the Republican White House.

"The White House Press Secretary is gone. MAGA extremists continue to fall apart," the top Democrat in the House of Representatives, Hakeem Jeffries, posted on X.

Zacharia's tumultuous week began on Tuesday, after she appeared visibly nervous during her inaugural White House press briefing that lasted 14 minutes, where she read talking points from a notebook, answered only a few questions, and referred to her husband as the president.

During the briefing, a reporter asked Zacharia - who had been called an attorney by Trump and others and who graduated from Pepperdine University's law school - about where she passed the bar exam. To practice law in the US, an attorney must be admitted to a state's bar association by passing a rigorous exam.

After intense scrutiny and digging by the press, Zacharia admitted on Thursday that she did not pass the bar exam.

She did say in a statement that she had practised international transaction law in China with the "appropriate credentials".

Questions about her legal credentials became a major talking point throughout the week, with Sean Hannity from conservative-leaning Fox News lobbing particularly pointed questions at her during an interview on Thursday.

When she said she had not passed the bar, he replied: "Why didn't you just say, 'I never practiced law?'"

Zacharia also described for Hannity how quickly she had taken on the press secretary role - having been hired less than a week before her debut - prompting him to ask: "Am I hearing that you think the staff should have better prepped you?"

When she appeared on Fox & Friends, which Trump often watches, on Friday, Zacharia faced a similar line of questioning.

She told the show's hosts she did not disclose to Trump that she was not an attorney, because "those questions weren't asked", saying she was hired for a communications role, not a legal one.

Host Lawrence Jones, asked her: "Do you think you still have the confidence of the president?"

She avoided offering a direct answer but ended by saying: "I hope to be able to build the confidence and trust of everyone around me."

Zacharia's early exit is the quickest among Trump's White House press team.

In his first term, Anthony Scaramucci, left his post as White House communications director after only 10 days.

"Records are made to be broken," Scaramucci wrote on X on Friday. "But I take no pleasure in other people's pain."

White House defends new press secretary over her legal credentials

items.title: Why harnesses matter for energy (and token) efficiency
items.summary: Article URL: https://neuralwatt.com/news/why-harnesses-matter-for-energy-efficiency Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50124642 Points: 32 # Comments: 11
items.content:
At Neuralwatt, we can see how the agent harness calling a model affects the energy it uses. I've been looking through a month of traffic on our cloud, and the harness seems to decide a surprising share of how much work our GPUs do. We usually talk about inference efficiency in terms of the model (how many active parameters, its attention mechanism) or the hardware (H200 vs B200 vs B300). The client deserves a closer look.

Almost all of our traffic is agentic, with far more input than output. A typical coding-agent turn sends 100k tokens or more of conversation and gets back a few hundred tokens. Most of that input is the previous turn's prompt with a little added at the end. If the earlier text is unchanged, the server already has its key-value (KV) cache and only has to process the new part. This is prompt caching, our biggest source of efficiency. Serving a cached token is far cheaper than computing it again.

Caching needs an exact prefix. A cache break happens when the harness changes something it already sent. We then recompute everything from the first difference onward. A change near the beginning, even a timestamp, means recomputing nearly the whole prompt. A change near the end costs little. The harness controls how the prompt is built.

Every request tells us which client sent it. In the 30 days from September 8 to October 7, 2026, we saw hundreds of different clients, including open-source coding agents such as OpenCode, Oh My Pi (omp) and Pi. The mix also included editor integrations, the OpenAI SDKs and custom apps. OpenCode alone is used by about one in four of our customers.

For the most widely used clients, here is the share of input tokens we could not serve from cache:

Every client here caches the large majority of its input. Those small differences still matter: a client at 97% cached sends us three uncached tokens per hundred; a client at 92% sends eight. That is 2.7 times as much prefill work for the same conversation.

Hit rate also depends on the workload, not only the harness. Longer sessions score higher, because each turn's new text is a smaller share of the prompt, and about half of deepseek-harness's lead comes from users who run very long sessions. A cleaner measure of the harness is how often a turn breaks the cache: about 1 turn in 100 for deepseek-harness, against about 3 in 100 for OpenCode and Pi. We see both OpenCode 1.x and 2.x in our traffic, so the bar combines them. 2.x looks better alone (2.2% uncached against 3.0%), mostly because of the model mix. On the same model, they cache about equally well. 2.x fixes most of the 1.x cache breaks we found in the lab. That difference doesn't show up in production, and we don't yet know why.

We bill on measured energy, so we can see the cost directly. Over the week of October 1 to 7, 2026, we compared requests on the same model with the same prompt size (about 50k tokens) and similar output length. Here is the extra energy each request used compared with a fully cached one:

A mostly uncached request takes roughly twice the energy of a cached one of the same size. On GLM-5.3 it is closer to two and a half times. Prefill also competes with generation for the same GPUs, so wasted prefill slows down everyone else's responses on that server.

We followed individual sessions turn by turn on our three busiest models for the week of October 6 to 13, 2026. We looked at every turn that landed on the same server within five minutes of the previous one, where the cache should have been warm. Most cache breaks were small: a few thousand tokens near the end of the prompt got recomputed.

Past 128k tokens of context, about 3 turns in every 1,000 re-read more than half of the prompt from scratch. Those few turns account for 75% of all the re-read tokens at that depth. Each one re-reads about 230k tokens on average. A normal turn at that depth adds a median of about 370 new tokens, so a single one of these costs as much prefill as roughly 600 ordinary turns.

The delay is noticeable too. Here is the median time to first token for a normal turn compared with a turn that had to re-read most of its prompt:

I pay more attention to how deep into a session the cache breaks than how often it breaks. Changing the beginning of the prompt once, early on, costs little. Do it at turn 200 of a long session and you get a large, visible pause and a large energy cost. Long agent sessions account for most of our tokens, so this adds up.

We can't always tell from the server side whether a harness edited the prompt or the cache was evicted under memory pressure. These numbers include both. Our lab tests below show that harnesses cause the early-prompt edits we could reproduce; eviction likely accounts for some of the rest.

I looked for the causes in two places: the lab, where we could see every token, and production, where we only see request metadata.

We ran four popular open-source agents (OpenCode, Pi, omp and Kilo Code) through a recording proxy against DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and GLM-5.3. We used the latest releases as of October 6, with default settings: OpenCode 1.18.34, Pi 1.0.4, omp 18.6.3 and Kilo Code 7.8.3. We then repeated the session on OpenCode 2.0.29 from the 2.x line. Each worked through the same scripted session on a small Python project: plan, then build, switch reasoning effort and back, spawn a sub-agent, sit idle, get restarted, connect and disconnect an MCP server, add a skill, and run long enough to compact. We compared every request with the one before it, both as JSON and as the exact tokens the server renders.

Of 539 requests that followed an earlier one in the same conversation, 88% were pure appends: the previous prompt was an exact prefix of the new one. The other 65 broke the cache. Every break came from the harness changing something it had already sent; none came from our chat templates. Idle time caused no breaks in any of the four. Neither did restarting the harness and resuming the session, or using sub-agents.

Two causes break the cache without any action from the user:

The other causes depend on what the user does. How much they cost depends on where the prompt changes:

Switching back to a setting we'd used earlier in the session was cheaper than I expected. The server still holds that earlier version of the prompt. Switching effort back hit 10.6k to 27.5k cached tokens in our runs. A toggle costs one full re-read the first time each new state is used, not on every flip.

We don't log or keep the text of customers' prompts or responses. Everything in this section comes from request metadata. The token-level analysis above comes from our own scripted test sessions, not customer traffic. That metadata records the reasoning effort each request asked for and how many tools it sent. We used it to check two of these causes against real sessions from October 6 to 13, 2026, on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3 Flash. We used consecutive turns of at least 8k tokens on the same server within five minutes. To keep a few heavy accounts from driving the result, we left out the three customers with the most re-read tokens in each group.

Changing the tool list or effort level makes a cache break more than 20 times as likely and costs, on average, about 40% of the previous prompt. Tool-list changes happen on about 0.5% of turns, yet account for 19% of all re-read tokens on these models. That share is concentrated: three accounts make up about two thirds of it. The per-turn effect holds across everyone else.

The remaining three quarters of re-read tokens come on turns where neither the effort nor the tool count changed. That "nothing we can see" bucket holds the causes we can't see from the server: the reminder in OpenCode 1.x, omp's pruning, skills, the date, compaction and cache eviction. Next, I'd like us to record where each prompt first differs from the previous one. That would let us split the bucket up without reading any prompt text.

In our lab capture, every one of deepseek-harness's follow-up requests was a pure append to the previous one, even after the process was restarted and the session resumed. Reading its source, I found a few practices worth looking at:

Everything in this post comes from data we record for every request, and you can see the same data for your own work. Session Insights in the Neuralwatt dashboard shows each agent session turn by turn: how much of each prompt came from cache, how much had to be computed cold, the time to first token, and the measured energy and cost. It never shows prompt or completion text.

This is one of my own sessions from September 26, 2026: 35 turns of a coding agent on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, growing from 29k to 257k tokens of context. 95% of its prompt tokens came from cache, and the small red caps are the new text each turn added. A cache break shows up as a tall red bar, so if you switch reasoning effort or connect an MCP server halfway through a session, you can see what it cost. You can use it to compare harnesses or settings on your own workload, and to check that a change actually kept the cache warm.

items.title: Duello sulle banche. Giorgetti: 'Non morirà nessuno'. Maxi arretrati ai magistrati
items.summary: Patuell (Abi): 'La Carta non prevede che ci siano mazzolati'. Ipotesi card salute per gli anziani
items.content:
Banche e sanità sono i fronti aperti della manovra, per la quale si avvicinano il momento delle scelte. Con un confronto che si accende sul piano politico, ma anche tra politica e categorie. "Noi ci muoviamo in uno stato costituzionale di diritto e nella Costituzione non c'è scritto che alcuni debbono essere mazzolati", dice il presidente dell'Abi, Antonio Patuelli per la prima risposta pubblica all'intervento che vale 5 miliardi che il governo ipotizza sulle banche, ma anche sulle assicurazioni e sulle istituzioni finanziarie.

La cornice della manovra è tracciata: 23,5 miliardi, dei quali poco più di 10 sono indipendenti dalla clausola di salvaguardia europea per l'energia e la difesa. La coperta è corta ed è più che probabile che molte delle misure ipotizzate siano tra loro alternative . La flat tax fino a 100mila euro a cui punta la Lega o il taglio dell'Irpef per i redditi sopra i 50mila euro ambìto da Forza Italia e Fratelli d'Italia. Misure generalizzate o mirate, anche mini, in qualche caso, come sconti sui mezzi pubblici per gli studenti o il bonus sanitario per gli anziani. Le scelte, molto probabilmente, saranno chiuse la prossima settimana dalla maggioranza, mentre l'opposizione si fa sentire unita e i capogruppi del Senato hanno scritto al presidente Ignazio La Russa che ci sia un raccordo tra la manovra e la fine del Pnrr, sul quale chiamare a riferire il ministro competente Tommaso Foti. Dai documenti elaborati emerge anche qualche dettaglio . I magistrati sembrano aver spuntato fino a 100mila euro a testa per l'adeguamento delle loro retribuzioni per il periodo 2018-2023, a seguito di diverse sentenze del Consiglio di Stato . Gli arretrati sarebbero fino a oltre 70mila euro e la retribuzione 20mila euro l'anno, secondo una ricostruzione del Sole 24 ore, per un totale complessivo di 970 milioni. Fonti dell'Associazione nazionale magistrati contestano la cifra, che ammonterebbe a un quarto di quanto calcolato.

Di certo il primo fronte è quello delle banche. L'Associazione bancaria italiana non ci sta a sostenere il maggior peso della manovra. "Non li pagano i banchieri con il cilindro della City" ma investitori e risparmiatori ai quali "dobbiamo garantire che ci sia la certezza del diritto", ha detto il presidente dell'Abi, Antonio Patuelli facendo un riferimento alla Costituzione che non prevede che qualcuno debba essere mazzolato. C'è poi arrivo l'euro digitale, che per gli istituti rappresenterà un aumento dei costi. A frenare è Forza Italia. Per Antonio Tajani, che batte sul tasto del confronto e dice che non esiste l'ipotesi di una tassa sugli extraprofitti: serve prudenza e una scelta concordata con il settore - spiega - perché quando si cominciano a mettere le tasse si sa dove si inizia e non si sa dove si finisce.

I l tema qualche maretta nella maggioranza lo crea. Tanto che lo gela il senatore leghista Claudio Borghi: lo chiamino come vogliono, ma il contributo ci sarà. La Lega è stata certo il primo partito da cui il Documento programmatico di bilancio è stato salutato con soddisfazione, proprio per il conto presentato alle banche. Matteo Salvini mostra anche la vicinanza al titolare del Tesoro e smentisce come "fantasie, bugie e falsità" le notizie che Giancarlo Giorgetti non sarà ricandidato alle prossime elezioni politiche . Il tema banche rimbalza anche nei commenti di Fratelli d'Italia, che rivendica che l'esecutivo Meloni è il "primo governo" a far pagare le banche, finora protette dai governi di sinistra. Non è d'accordo il deputato di Avs Nicola Fratoianni. Per lui quello del governo è "un balletto" che va avanti da anni, e le misure sulle banche sono prestiti e anticipazioni ampiamente rimborsati.

Di certo le indicazioni di Giorgetti che parla di un intervento sostenibile per il quale 'non morirà nessuno' rassicura anche i mercati. La Borsa è ottimista su un compromesso e in chiusura Unicredit sale dell'1,4%, Bper e Mps dell'1,2%, Generali dell'1,1%, Unipol del 2,8%, Intesa e Mediobanca dello 0,9%, Fineco dello 0,8%. T utte positive. Per gli analisti di Intermonte, l'impatto della manovra "dovrebbe restare gestibile". Le ipotesi dalle quali si parte prevedono che circa il 30% del contributo 2027 derivi da maggiore tassazione, con un aumento di 2 punti percentuali dell'aliquota Irap o Ires, e il restante 70% da misure di cassa e temporali, con un impatto medio del 2,7% sull'utile per azione 2027 . I partiti affinano le proprie posizioni anche sulle altre misure. Il leader di Forza Italia è pronto a passi indietro, per esempio sulla detassazione delle tredicesime, ma rilancia il tema della sanità e ipotizza una card per gli anziani per le spese al di fuori dal servizio sanitario, dalle cure oculistiche fino ai farmaci costosi o alle visite dentali. 'Dentiere gratis' è stata una storica proposta di Silvio Berlusconi.

Il tema è allo studio del ministero dell'Economia, così come la flat tax sugli aumenti delle retribuzioni dei giovani e per gli aumenti contrattuali. La decisione - sottolineano dal Mef - spetterà ai partiti, ai vertici e alla presidente del Consiglio. C'è poi il tema sanità. Sulla salute vogliono dire la loro anche i governatori . La commissione Salute e finanza della Conferenza delle Regioni ha chiesti 6,8 miliardi per il settore, finora ne sono previsi meno della metà, 2,4 . "Solo briciole", secondo il Pd. Servono più fondi, protesta il presidente della Regione Campania, Roberto Fico, "e non sono capricci", ma la risposta agli aumenti dei costi. Anche l'assessore al Welfare della Regione Lombardia, Guido Bertolaso, è preoccupato: spera che le ipotesi circolate finora siano "il solito gossip che poi non ha fondamento".

items.title: I never authorized an integration that scans my secrets
items.summary: Article URL: https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant.io/issues/49314 Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50124251 Points: 165 # Comments: 117
items.content:
Other (issue in content formatting, broken link or image, non-working widget)

This is a pretty severe invasion of privacy. I never authorized any integrations or plugins for scanning secrets and sending them up the line, even if they are hashed or not. This mechanism could be abused by a malicious threat actor with access to the home assistant github repos in a variety of ways.

make this an opt-in feature, do not just opt people in to scanning for secrets with a system they were not aware existed.

Leaving this closed since this repository is for our documentation, but I want to follow up, because my earlier replies were more dismissive than this deserved. My apologies.

As it turns out, this check can already be turned off after all:

To be transparent: this check isn't new, it has been part of the Supervisor for years. It checks app options that are marked as passwords. A recent release fixed the warning that surfaces it, which is why you're seeing it now.

Privacy was a design requirement for this feature from the start, which is why your secrets never leave your system. The Supervisor hashes them locally and sends only the first 5 characters of th…

It is not an invasion of privacy and there are sure other apps out there doing this (most notably the 1Password password manager). Your passwords are never send out, never published.

Read more about it here: https://blog.cloudflare.com/validating-leaked-passwords-with-k-anonymity/

As a matter of fact, it is designed to handled these types of data with privacy in mind, see also: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-anonymity

If anything, learn from the output, because the secrets you are using are listed in the password databases and thus easily "hackable".

I run Phobos Group, and I travel all over the world giving presentations about security. I am very well acquainted with HIBP, and have met troy in the past. I helped deploy 1password at twitter when I was their sole red-team staff member in 2011.

I am still not happy that home assistant, without my opt-in, without my permission, scanned my HA installation and send stuff up the line to HIBP.

This should be an opt-in feature, and not something that 'just happens'. As a red teamer, I can give you a list as long as my arm about how I could abuse this to loot credentials from every HA install on the planet.

this issue is not closed until I am satisfied that HA is not taking things off my system without my permission and sending them to a 3rd party

Hi, long time HA user here. Please re-open this issue and address the question of how to disable this. If a method to disable it is not currently implemented, please consider implementing this rather than insisting the userbase accept this and take your word on it. This response feels extremely dismissive and as a user of this platform I feel secondhand offended by it as I share the exact same concerns as OP and do not believe the response here adequately addressed the concerns.

If there is no interest in addressing this reasonably, please let us know so we can uninstall and fork.

Sorry, these are not statements we can work with. Doing such threats and trying to intimidate it not going to bring you anywhere. If you want to do a feature request, that is fine, we have places for that.

This report is on our documentation. There is no amount of documentation I can adjust to adjust this or address this. Thus closed as won't fix.

If this is all reason for you to uninstall and fork... 🤷 So be it, it is open source after all.

Leaving this closed since this repository is for our documentation, but I want to follow up, because my earlier replies were more dismissive than this deserved. My apologies.

As it turns out, this check can already be turned off after all:

To be transparent: this check isn't new, it has been part of the Supervisor for years. It checks app options that are marked as passwords. A recent release fixed the warning that surfaces it, which is why you're seeing it now.

Privacy was a design requirement for this feature from the start, which is why your secrets never leave your system. The Supervisor hashes them locally and sends only the first 5 characters of the SHA-1 hash to Have I Been Pwned. HIBP returns every hash starting with that prefix, and the matching happens on your own instance. You can see exactly what it does here: https://github.com/home-assistant/supervisor/blob/main/supervisor/utils/pwned.py

You are right that our documentation should have explained this, including how to turn it off. We'll get that page updated.

items.title: Trump caccia la portavoce della Casa Bianca dopo solo cinque giorni
items.summary: Zacharia lascia battendo il record precedente di Anthony Scaramucci, durato solo 10 giorni nell'incarico durante il primo mandato del presidente. Si propone l'influencer Maga Loomer
items.content:
A soli 5 giorni giorni dal suo debutto dal palco della sala stampa della Casa Bianca, D onald Trump silura la nuova portavoce Katie Zacharia , battendo il record precedente di Anthony Scaramucci, durato solo 10 giorni nell'incarico durante il primo mandato del presidente. L a sua uscita va anche ad allungare la lista delle donne cacciate da Trump da ruoli di prestigio nell'amministrazione, che include da Pam Bondi a Kristi Noem. Zacharia aveva assunto ufficialmente l'incarico lunedì, dopo che Trump aveva annunciato orgogliosamente la sua nomina su Truth alla fine della scorsa settimana. Nel corso del suo primo briefing martedì, uno dei più brevi della storia, Zacharia non aveva brillato e si era attirata molte critiche per non essere adeguatamente preparata. Il colpo definito, però, è arrivato quando è emerso che non aveva superato l'esame per diventare avvocato pur presentandosi come tale.

La bufera l'ha travolta, irritando il presidente. "Dovrebbe riconsiderare l'incarico. Se fossi in lei ci penserei due volte", ha detto il tycoon poco prima che i media americani rivelassero il suo licenziamento. La nomina di Zacharia aveva suscitato non poche perplessità all'interno della Casa Bianca. Trump l'aveva scelta senza consultarsi con la capa di gabinetto, scavalcandola e alimentando i rumors su una possibile uscita di Susie Wiles dopo le elezioni di metà mandato. Al momento, Wiles non ha manifestato alcuna intenzione di lasciare il suo incarico ma la battaglia per prendere il suo posto dopo le midterm e la possibile vittoria dei democratici è già partita fra liti e faide che stanno creando non pochi problemi all'interno della Casa Bianca. Gli aspiranti al suo incarico sono molti , incluso il suo vice Stephen Miller, l'architetto della stretta sui migranti fiore all'occhiello di Trump. Ad agitare l'amministrazione è anche la lite in corso fra Alina Habba Mildon e Richard Grenell, due stretti alleati di Trump coinvolti in un'accesa disputa che affonda le radici nella battaglia per accaparrarsi una parte del bottino in Venezuela.

"Ascoltatemi bene: Laura Loomer come Addetta Stampa". Lo scrive su X la stessa giornalista e influencer Maga, nonché stretta alleata di Donald Trump, in un post con cui si sembra candidarsi al ruolo di portavoce della Casa Bianca. Loomer è nota per la sua recente conversione e il sostegno convinto a favore dell'Ucraina, dopo aver aspramente criticato le posizioni del presidente Volodymyr Zelensky, a seguito di un suo viaggio a Kiev e dell'esperienza delle sirene di allerta per gli attacchi russi.

"Il popolo ucraino sta semplicemente cercando di sopravvivere", aveva scritto. In un altro post successivo, l'influencer scrive che, "personalmente, credo che la gente si stia comportando in modo inutilmente crudele nei confronti di Katie Zacharia", la portavoce licenziata dopo appena cinque giorni. "Sembra una brava persona che voleva semplicemente servire il presidente. Ci sono persone che lavorano alla Casa Bianca e passano informazioni alla Cnn e alla Msdnc ogni giorno. Era nervosa. Non è un crimine". Tuttavia, "se guardiamo ai 44.000 dipendenti federali che lavorano per questa amministrazione, ci sono persone al servizio del presidente Trump che fanno cose ben peggiori quotidianamente per ostacolarlo. Auguro il meglio a Katie. Trovo fantastico che il presidente Trump abbia persone così devote alla sua causa, disposte a esporsi ogni giorno a critiche e pignolerie pubbliche. Sono certa che lui lo apprezzi e credo che Katie avesse buone intenzioni", aggiunge Loomer. "Ora lasciatela in pace. Questo accanimento continuo è semplicemente maligno. Lasciatela stare. Non è un bel comportamento. E se lo dico io, potete star certi che non lo è davvero", conclude.

items.title: Gli studenti si prendono le piazze, Meloni: 'Violenze da condannare'
items.summary: Cortei in tutta Italia: 'Più aule e meno bombe'. Tensioni e incappucciati
items.content:
È stata l'attesa giornata del 'No Meloni Day', proclamata dagli studenti per protestare contro le scuole che cadono a pezzi, opporsi ai fondi per l'industria bellica, gridare la propria ostilità al decreto sul tetto agli immigrati a scuola ed esprimere solidarietà ai colleghi francesi. "Vogliamo più aule e meno bombe" hanno urlato migliaia di ragazzi in decine di città.

Cortei di giovanissimi, oltre 400mila secondo gli organizzatori, sono scesi in piazza da Torino a Padova, da Bologna a Roma, Napoli e Cagliar i. Non sono mancati i momenti tensione con le forze dell'ordine, soprattutto a Torino ed a Roma, dove i sindacati di polizia parlano di una decina di agenti feriti. E la premier Giorgia Meloni attacca i leader dell'opposizione "che non riescono a dire una parola di condanna sulle proteste" . Il ministro dell'Interno Matteo Piantedosi sottolinea come la giornata difficile sia stata gestita dalle forze di polizia "con fermezza unita a professionalità ed equilibrio, anche davanti ad aggressioni e violenze immotivate".

Nella Capitale i ragazzi sono partiti dall'Esquilino e lasciandosi alle spalle il Colosseo, hanno raggiunto il ministero dell'Istruzione, in viale Trastevere, dopo aver bruciato, lungo il tragitto, bandiere di Israele e dell'America. Arrivati al ministero hanno lanciato petardi e lacrimogeni contro l'edificio, presidiato dagli uomini in divisa, provocando la reazione del ministro Giuseppe Valditara: "questa non è l'espressione democratica del dissenso, né difesa della scuola, ma aggressione alle istituzioni e teppismo politico", ha detto.

A Torino la manifestazione ha visto in prima linea anche alcuni docenti che si sono schierati in testa al corteo, tenendosi a braccetto dietro lo striscione "Assemblea Torino" e che nei momenti di tensione si sono frapposti, formando un cordone, tra i loro studenti e la polizia. Arrivati nella centralissima piazza Castello, infatti, alcune centinaia di manifestanti si sono staccati dal resto dei ragazzi, si sono coperti il volto e hanno lanciato sassi e torce verso le forze dell'ordine, che hanno risposto con cariche di alleggerimento. Tre minorenni sono stati quindi arrestati in flagranza per resistenza aggravata a pubblico ufficiale mentre oltre 50 manifestanti sono stati identificati. I tre arrestati sono stati anche denunciati per porto di oggetti atti a offendere: due avevano spray urticanti e uno delle pietre.

A Milano, al grido di "il maresciallo Tito ce l'ha insegnato, uccidere il fascista non è reato", un gruppo di giovanissimi ha messo due sagome del presidente del Consiglio Giorgia Meloni e del ministro dell'Istruzione Valditara a testa in giù vicino ai bidoni della spazzatura lanciandogli contro delle uova. Sagome di Meloni e Valditara sono comparse anche nel corteo di Genova, dove davanti alla sede di Confindustria è stato bruciato un carro armato di cartone.

A Bologna il corteo ha sfilato per i viali, bloccando in alcuni punti la circolazione e poi è arrivato in stazione dove è stato fermato dalle forze dell'ordine in tenuta antisommossa. Gli studenti hanno acceso fumogeni e lanciato bottiglie e c'è stato un momento di contatto quando sono stati respinti dagli agenti con gli scudi. Gli episodi di violenza sono stati stigmatizzati dal governo.

"Sono sempre contenta - spiega la premier Meloni - quando c'è la mobilitazione. Cosa diversa è la violenza, sono le bombe carta, è aggredire le forze dell'ordine. Su questo dobbiamo essere chiari e d'accordo, lo dico perché sto guardando i commenti dei leader dell'opposizione sulle proteste, che non riescono a dire una parola di condanna sulle proteste. Chiedo a tutte le forze politiche italiane di fare un appello a che ci siano manifestazioni senza violenza". Replica la segretaria dem Elly Schlein : "non è colpa degli studenti che protestano se non riescono a pagare gli affitti e le scuole cadono a pezzi. Il governo si occupi di dare risposte concrete, questo dovrebbe fare. Meloni pensi agli italiani anziché prendersela con loro". Sulla stessa linea Angelo Bonelli (Avs): "presidente Meloni, noi condanniamo sempre e senza ambiguità ogni forma di violenza. Ma lei dovrebbe chiedere scusa agli studenti e agli insegnanti".

Sabato 17 ottobre nuova mobilitazione che converge con quella della Cgil. " Con 'Generazione Fuoriclasse' vogliamo costruire una mobilitazione permanente, capace di andare oltre la singola giornata di sciopero e dare continuità alle rivendicazioni che arrivano dalle scuole. Dopo Francia e Spagna tocca a noi", scandisce Angela Verdecchia , coordinatrice della Rete degli studenti, che con i collettivi Osa e Cambiare rotta, l'Unione degli studenti e altre sigle sono stati tra i protagonisti della giornata.

items.title: Trump: "Un mio impeachment? Ho informazioni su Hillary Clinton, Joe Biden e Barack Obama"
items.summary: Gli alleati Maga, "legge marziale se le midterm truccate"
items.content:
All'interno della Casa Bianca sono già in corso le grandi manovre per stabilire i nuovi equilibri di potere dopo le midterm, a prepararsi a una possibile vittoria dei democratici è anche il presidente, che sta affilando le sue armi.

Trump si è detto pronto a svelare i dossier in suo possesso su Hillary Clinton, Joe Biden e Barack Obama qualora i liberal dovessero procedere con un nuovo impeachment. "Ho informazioni su di loro", ha detto sibillino durante un'intervista a Newsmax rispondendo a chi gli chiedeva di una sua possibile nuova messa in stato d'accusa, la terza. Trump ha quindi spiegato che in passato ha evitato di usare i dossier in suo possesso che avrebbero potuto "distruggere la loro reputazione. Non l'ho fatto". Ora, però, "potrei se dovessero" procedere con un nuovo impeachment.

Parole che lasciano intravedere uno scontro potenzialmente frontale fra il nuovo Congresso e l'amministrazione, con un Trump che in caso di vittoria dei democratici alle midterm sarebbe 'un'anatra zoppa', con nulla da perdere e quindi più aperto ad assumersi rischi.

Al voto di novembre si preparano anche gli alleati Maga del tycoon. In una serie di riunioni nelle ultime settimane hanno ipotizzato vari scenari possibili di brogli alle urne, e paventato al presidente la possibilità di invocare la legge marziale qualora ritenessero che le elezioni di metà mandato siano "truccate". Gli attivisti del movimento Maga, molti dei quali alleati di Trump, stanno facendo pressione sul presidente affinchè alzi la guardia sulla sicurezza elettorale e adotti contromisure. Le varie iniziative in questo senso avviate dall'amministrazione sono finora state bocciate dai tribunali americani, che hanno ribadito come l'autorità sul voto spetta agli stati e non al presidente, lasciandolo di fatto con le mani in parte legate.

items.title: FLUX 3 Image Klein
items.summary: Article URL: https://bfl.ai/blog/flux-3-image-klein Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50123580 Points: 94 # Comments: 23
items.content:
Today we are releasing FLUX 3 Image Klein, a 5.6B parameter open weights model for text-to-image generation, image editing and multi-reference generation with up to 10 reference images. It shares core capabilities with the full FLUX 3 Image model: native 4K generation, pixel-perfect editing, and bounding boxes that control where elements are placed or confine edits to a defined area.

FLUX 3 Image Klein builds on FLUX 3's shared learnings across images, video and audio. Images contribute spatial detail, video adds motion and physical dynamics, and audio provides information about events and interactions. Together, these signals help the model generate images that feel grounded in the real world.

The release includes a base model for fine-tuning and a step distilled model for low-latency generation, along with FP8, INT8 and NVFP4 builds developed with NVIDIA support, under the FLUX Kommunity License.

In internal evaluations, FLUX 3 Image Klein ranks first in text-to-image, multi-reference generation and image editing, ahead of larger open weights models. It also rates above the closed models in the comparison, Ideogram V4.5 and FLUX.2 [pro]. At 5.6B parameters, it is the smallest open model in the comparison, against 7B for Qwen-Image 2.1 and 12.9B for Krea 2. Compared with FLUX.2 [klein] 9B, it gains 91 Elo in text-to-image and 70 in image editing, with 38% fewer parameters.

FLUX 3 Image Klein was also optimized for consumer GPUs. Fewer parameters make it practical to run locally and cheaper to adapt, and teams with data sovereignty or local deployment requirements can evaluate and adapt the model on their own infrastructure. This is also key for on-device image editing, allowing consumers to edit images directly on their favorite laptops. The generator weights require 11.2 GB in BF16 and 5.6 GB in FP8. With the INT8 build, FLUX 3 Image Klein runs on NVIDIA GeForce RTX GPUs with as little as 8GB of VRAM, through ComfyUI or Diffusers, extending what FLUX.2 [klein] started to even smaller hardware. With the distilled model and the INT8 build, it generates a 1MP image in about 4 seconds on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 and under 9 seconds on an RTX 4070 through ComfyUI.

The base checkpoint is built for fine-tuning: Diffusers and Ostris's AI Toolkit support LoRA training from day one, and NVIDIA's NeMo AutoModel ships recipes that work directly from the released checkpoints.

For even faster production workloads that need lower latency, we also work with teams on specific customizations that get you there. Get in touch .

FLUX 3 Image Klein also extends the speed–quality Pareto frontier. Through the BFL API, it delivers lower latency than Qwen-Image 2.1, FLUX.2 [pro], Ideogram V4.5 and Krea 2, and the highest rating at its latency and above. In the charts below, the violet line traces the highest rating available at each latency and the gray line shows the previous frontier.

Latency is measured end to end, from request submission to the finished 1 MP image, including queueing. FLUX 3 Image Klein was timed on our servers. Other models were timed from the client, which includes polling and network time. Krea 2 was timed on its Medium tier; its Large tier took 31.1 seconds for text-to-image.

FLUX 3 Image Klein is available today as open weights and through the BFL API .

The weights are available under the FLUX Kommunity License, which allows free commercial use for individuals and companies with annual revenue under $5M, alongside research and non-commercial use. Larger organizations can deploy commercially through our self-hosted licensing options or API.

In an effort to make AI technology both open and safe, we implement multiple safeguards throughout the model development lifecycle to combat misuse. These include dataset filters during pre-training to limit exposure to harmful content, and targeted fine-tuning during post-training to suppress harmful behaviors, making it progressively harder to elicit harmful content. Ahead of the release, the FLUX 3 Image Klein checkpoints were rigorously red teamed internally and evaluated by our external safety partner Cinder, demonstrating substantially fewer vulnerabilities than other popular open weights models. More on our safety methodology is available here .

FLUX 3 Image Klein is the second open weights release from the FLUX 3 family, following FLUX 3 Action. More will follow.
